name: Arctic Species Conservation Fund
summary: Small rolling grants for stewardship and research on Canadian Arctic wildlife and habitat, such as Indigenous protected area work, caribou and polar bear conflict projects, and marine mammal studies. Nunavut projects are prioritised.
reporting: Up to three items: an interim report after the first major milestone, communications media in some cases, and a final report with a financial statement.

steps: Proposal by email, at least six weeks before project start
Proposal review, with results in four to six weeks

documents: Community support letter if the applicant does not represent the local Indigenous organization
Full project budget, with secured and unsecured funding from other sources

status.quote: Proposals will be accepted and reviewed on a rolling basis at any point in the year.

applicant_types.quote: Applicants from all backgrounds (community groups, Hunters and Trappers Organizations, governments, universities, independent researchers, non-government organizations, etc.)

geography.quote: Projects can take place anywhere across northern Canada, though projects based in Nunavut will be prioritized.

access.quote: Applications should be submitted in PDF format to

window.quote: Proposals will be accepted and reviewed on a rolling basis at any point in the year.

amount.quote: Applicants can request up to $25,000 per year.

reporting.quote: Successful recipients will submit up to three reporting items during the project period: a) Interim report Roughly one month after the completion of the first major project milestone

effort.quote: Final proposals should be submitted at least six weeks prior to the project start date.
Applications should be submitted to arcticspecies@wwfcanada.org.
Applicants will be notified of the results of their proposal within four to six weeks of receipt.

after_award.quote: Roughly one month after the completion of the first major project milestone, recipients will be required to submit an interim report following a WWF-Canada template outlining the implementation of the project, preliminary results, updated work plan and a financial report of funds spent to date.

documents.quote: Relevance to northern communities, involvement of northern residents in the project and a letter of support from a representative community organization if applicable
Full project budget, including secured and unsecured funding from other sources, and a detailed indication of how WWF-Canada funds will be used
must demonstrate community support for the project through a letter of support if the applicant is not a representative of the local Indigenous organization.
